Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll start with the workspace contract in `README.md`, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence and both wake views before proposing the single candidate. I’ll also follow the fish-control bookshelf transfer protocol and record any actual transfer explicitly in the policy notes.

The workspace requires `guidance/README.md` and the inherited control experience before edits. I’m also consulting the two applicable local skills now: the bookshelf protocol the task names, and the wake-visual inspection procedure that governs policy changes here.

The inherited experience shows this is a later capture-stage iteration, not the common seed: steering, posterior reserve, continuous stopping risk, and a smooth acceleration envelope already produced capture. I’ll compare the strongest sampled capture with the most informative contrasting capture, including both visual rows and diagnostics, before deciding whether the bookshelf’s re-consultation trigger applies.

The scalar summaries confirm all sampled runs captured under direct uniform still water, so the useful contrast is mechanical quality rather than success/failure: the `16.943T`, `−0.2054` run versus the slower or higher-load captures. I’m now extracting comparable trajectory/load/saturation fields and reading the parent’s inherited policy notes so the next mechanism is tied to evidence rather than score alone.

Both tested speed guards eliminated exact `260°/T` occupancy, but they paid for it: the parent’s one-sided guard arrived at `17.330T` (versus `16.943T`), while the stronger linear barrier arrived at `17.435T` and reduced peak swim speed further. Their alternating wakes remain coherent, so this is a concrete control tradeoff, not wake collapse. I’m consulting the bookshelf’s primitive map now for a mechanism-level way to protect velocity without repeating simple near-limit gain suppression; if it informs the edit, I’ll include the required transfer block.

The evidence exposes a useful phase relationship: in the best soft-envelope trace, the joints never hit the speed limit simultaneously. During all 115 anterior-limit samples the posterior joint remains below 90% speed (mean about 27% of its limit), and during all 109 posterior-limit samples the anterior also remains below 90%. I’m recording a single-candidate hypothesis that keeps the milder proven speed guard but sends only a bounded portion of anterior work it removes into the speed-safe posterior carrier phase; this tests whether limit protection can retain propulsion without changing the target route or adding static curvature.

The candidate and durable guidance are both updated. The policy retains the successful target-course/soft-envelope/angle-safety stack, adds the inherited high-speed guard, and bounds the new one-way posterior allocation by both carrier sign and remaining acceleration headroom. I’m moving into contract validation now—parameter ownership, syntax-level structure, editable scope, and the mandated check-runner; I will not run CFD.

The mandated check-runner was invoked, but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unsupported in this environment, so it could not start. I’m executing the same three non-CFD checks locally and will repair any failure before finishing.

The guidance check found a rendered-workspace bookkeeping defect: `README.md` marks the same guidance parent twice, so the checker cannot identify one assigned parent. I’m removing only the duplicate marker (the same repair documented in the inherited parent log), then rerunning the semantic comparison.

The semantic guidance check and solver boundary check pass. Julia is not installed, so the executable smoke test cannot run; I’m compensating with deterministic static checks of every `params.FIELD`, delimiter balance, and finite/bounded branch structure, then reviewing the final diff against the prefilled policy.

Static contract checks pass, and the new mechanism is bounded. I’m doing one final evidence replay against the strongest trace—not CFD—to ensure the allocation is neither inert nor pervasive: how often it would activate, how much posterior headroom it would use, and whether its guard remains active only near the measured speed boundary.

Final validation is clean where tooling is available: guidance semantic PASS, solver boundary PASS, parameter-schema PASS, delimiter balance PASS, and exactly one candidate file. The evidence replay shows the added allocation is selective—active in about `6.62%` of the strongest trace, averaging `0.835 rad/T²`—so it is a real but bounded mechanism. The only unavailable check is Julia execution because the runtime is absent; no CFD was run.

Completed exactly one multi-wake policy candidate:

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): adds bounded phase-aware anterior-to-posterior work reallocation to the speed-viable soft-envelope controller.
- [Evidence, hypothesis, and bookshelf transfer](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [Reusable control lesson](guidance/control_experience.md:165)

Validation:

- Guidance semantic check: PASS
- Solver boundary check: PASS
- Parameter-schema and delimiter checks: PASS
- Exactly one candidate file: PASS
- Formal CFD: intentionally not run
- Check-runner was invoked but its pinned model is unsupported; its checks were run locally. Julia smoke testing was unavailable because Julia is not installed.

I also removed the duplicate assigned-parent marker from [README.md](README.md:120), which had prevented the guidance checker from identifying one parent.
